claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x, the distinguished-points Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md succeeds with probability at least 0.40005 using at most 2^128.08376 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^104.59 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^12 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice, quantum steps, or random-oracle premises. Success relies on the supported random-mapping heuristic for the r-adding walk, disclosed and supported in proof.md. This is an analytic best-known-attack cost analysis, not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Run the identical attack path on the fixed prime-order toy curve (n=9883) and measure success rate against the birthday prediction. This does not establish production curve behavior or cost bounds.
